factProposals.value: Completed care is not stored a second time: the clinical history is derived on every read from the completion rows that completing a plan procedure already writes (append-only state rows, one history event and one audit entry per procedure). A procedure appears once, with the plan revision in force when it was completed, and stays listed when its plan is later revised or withdrawn.

Dentists and administrators complete a plan's accepted procedures; the administrator, dentist, hygienist and assistant read the clinical history; front desk, billing and the office manager cannot, and anonymous callers get 401. Completing needs a CSRF token and the plan's current version.

Completing an accepted plan is all-or-nothing: a stale or missing version, a withdrawn plan, a plan with nothing accepted, and a failed audit write each complete nothing and say so ('Nothing was completed'); a replay or double click changes nothing; two simultaneous completions leave each procedure completed once.

Every completed procedure writes a history event and a PHI-free audit entry with the signed-in user and a timestamp in the same save as the completion, so a completion cannot exist without its log entry; a failed save shows no audit or SQL wording and logs only the error class and SQL error number.

decisions.statement: The clinical history is a read-only view of existing completion records, not a new table.
decisions.rationale: A second record of completed care could drift from the plan that holds the authoritative completion; deriving it keeps one source of truth, and the later completion story (ALV-008-C01) can introduce its own completed-procedure record deliberately.

decisions.statement: Plan-level completion completes every accepted open procedure at once; choosing a subset, charging and the odontogram update were left to ALV-008-C01.
decisions.rationale: The story's stop conditions are the three criteria; the master execution plan places the atomic completion with charges and odontogram in the next item, which builds on the ledger contract.

limitations.statement: A procedure completed by mistake cannot be undone (completed is final by design) and the history shows only planned care that was completed, not care that was never planned.
The completion records who and when from the signed-in account; there is no separate performing provider or procedure date until ALV-008-C01.
